classification.difficultyReason: Read the bounds, integrate each polynomial and negate the signed integral because the shaded region lies below the x-axis. This is direct application of the taught negative-area adjustment without splitting.

content.prompt: Find the area of each shaded region below by evaluating the appropriate integral.

spec.description: Upward-opening parabola with labelled intercepts and the region below the x-axis shaded light blue.
spec.mathematics: y=x^2-4x+3; x-intercepts 1 and 3; y-intercept 3; shade 1≤x≤3 between the curve and the x-axis.
spec.answerVisibility: The shaded region and printed graph labels are permanent givens; no calculated area is displayed.

answer.worked:
The shaded region lies below the $x$-axis.
$$\begin{align*}A&=-\int_1^3(x^2-4x+3)\,dx\\&=-\left[\frac{x^3}{3}-2x^2+3x\right]_1^3\\&=-\left[(9-18+9)-\left(\frac13-2+3\right)\right]\\&=\frac43\text{ units}^2.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Straight line through the origin with a shaded triangular region below the x-axis and a vertical boundary at x=-3.
spec.mathematics: y=3x; shade the region bounded by x=-3, y=0 and y=3x.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied graph, boundary label and shading are visible.

answer.worked:
The shaded region lies below the $x$-axis.
$$\begin{align*}A&=-\int_{-3}^0 3x\,dx\\&=-\left[\frac{3x^2}{2}\right]_{-3}^0\\&=-\left(0-\frac{27}{2}\right)\\&=\frac{27}{2}\text{ units}^2.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Cubic through the origin, with the negative region between x=-3 and x=0 shaded light blue.
spec.mathematics: y=x^3; shade -3≤x≤0 between the curve and the x-axis, retaining the vertical boundary at x=-3.
spec.answerVisibility: The function, boundary label and shaded region are supplied; the area is hidden.

answer.worked:
The shaded region lies below the $x$-axis.
$$\begin{align*}A&=-\int_{-3}^0 x^3\,dx\\&=-\left[\frac{x^4}{4}\right]_{-3}^0\\&=-\left(0-\frac{81}{4}\right)\\&=\frac{81}{4}\text{ units}^2.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Equation-driven quartic with independent horizontal and vertical scales, retaining the maximum label 1, positive intercept 1, boundary 3 and shaded negative region. The source graph is schematic.
spec.mathematics: y=1-x^4; maximum (0,1); positive root x=1; boundary x=3; shade 1≤x≤3 between the curve and the x-axis.
spec.answerVisibility: All printed givens and shading remain visible; no area answer is supplied in the student diagram.

answer.worked:
The shaded region lies below the $x$-axis.
$$\begin{align*}A&=-\int_1^3(1-x^4)\,dx\\&=-\left[x-\frac{x^5}{5}\right]_1^3\\&=-\left[\left(3-\frac{243}{5}\right)-\left(1-\frac15\right)\right]\\&=\frac{232}{5}\\&=46\frac25\text{ units}^2.\end{align*}$$
